To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“We know strikingly little of the impacts of livelihoods and economic interventions in conflictaffected environments, and programme choices often appear to have been driven by assumptions of success and unsubstantiated stories of success”.

■ The evidence base on the impact of livelihood interventions in conflict- affected environments is comprised of four categories: i) case study evidence of the effectiveness or otherwise of specific interventions; ii) evidence on the impact of economic growth on livelihoods and conflict; iii) evidence on the relationship between livelihoods and conflict in general; and iv) the impact of livelihoods and economic growth interventions in conflict- and post- conflict settings.

we know very little about the impacts, effectiveness and outcomes of livelihoods and economic interventions in conflict affected environments, and programming decisions are often made on the basis of unsubstantiated narratives.
